Independent symbolic adjugate/Cayley–Hamilton simplification and exact witness determinant calculation
correctness.rationale: On the stated finite-variance domain, the positive stationary moment vector satisfies (2K−Q)m=2Dπ and the covariance is 1ᵀ exp(t(Q−K))m. The two decay rates are distinct and positive, and the slow coefficient is strictly positive by the positive Perron projection. Independently used Cayley–Hamilton, C″(0)=−tr(Q−K)D−det(Q−K)V, and the adjugate moment formula to verify exactly that VC″(0)−D² is a strictly negative prefactor times the displayed F. It also equals the weight product times the squared rate difference. If the fast weight is negative, sufficiently high signed derivatives at zero are negative; nonnegative weights suffice at every lag. The quadratic has F(L)>0 and, whenever k>h and β≤βc, vertex strictly above L. Its vertex discriminates zero, one, or two admissible zeros as claimed. For k≤h the vertex is at or below L. At cancellation V=2D/(α+β), so the surviving (slow) rate is (α+β)/2. At both exact witness points det(2K−Q)>0 and det(4K−Q)<0: the latter gives positive spectral abscissa for Q−4K, incompatible with a finite stationary fourth-moment vector satisfying (4K−Q)n=12Dm (test with the positive left Perron vector). Thus the witness does not depend on taking a numerical tail fit. The stated exact general moment cutoff also agrees with the identified prior result.
residual_risks: The positive quantity called the Lyapunov exponent in the proof is the mean restoring coefficient; the homogeneous growth exponent has the opposite sign. The argument correctly uses contraction.
No formal verification or claims beyond stationary second-order covariance are implied.

originality.rationale: Qualified pass for the complete finite-variance phase diagram with a repulsive state and the two-boundary covariance/moment contrast. Neither the covariance propagator, the cancellation polynomial as algebra, nor the marginal tail cutoff is new. Close positive and on/off results do not include the repulsive admissibility domain or the reentrant band; finite-variance admissibility and the combination with divergent fourth moments are decisive.
residual_risks: A directly equivalent signed-stiffness coefficient analysis could exist under random-coefficient or telegraph-noise terminology outside the inspected works.
The most material near-coverage risk is the exact continuation of the positive-stiffness polynomial; no novelty is credited to the polynomial itself.

value.rationale: Repulsion gives a natural change of stability and integrability rather than an arbitrary parameter slice. The exhaustive empty/singleton/bounded-band alternative answers when every covariance derivative has the equilibrium-mixture sign, even when the covariance stays positive outside. The two distinct all-lag OU matches with infinite fourth moments give a concrete limit on identification from even perfect second-order statistics, not just from a fitted decay rate.
residual_risks: The contrast is about covariance and moments only; it establishes neither equal response nor statistical indistinguishability with other data.
